explainBack.question: If Claude 'led' 26% of Anthropic's AI research work, why doesn't that mean the AI is doing research autonomously?
explainBack.answer: Because 'led' is defined as completing most of a defined task from a high-level prompt while a human supervises. A human still chose the task, framed the prompt, watched the work and judged the output. Full autonomy would remove the human from that loop entirely, and Anthropic says no measured subset reached that level. So 26% measures how much bounded execution was handed over, not who holds authority over goals, evidence or deployment.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: The reader should cite the AL4 definition (high-level prompt plus human supervision), the AL5 absence claim, and the goal/judgment/deployment rights remaining human.
explainBack.assessment: The article supports this answer fully: P004 supplies the level definitions, P002 the 26%/none figures, and P005 the retained human decision rights, so the causal explain-back is accurate and grounded.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A pharmaceutical company announces that its AI system 'independently ran 70% of drug-candidate screening experiments last quarter' and a headline claims the AI is 'discovering drugs on its own'.
unseenTransfer.question: Using this article's mechanism, how should a reader evaluate whether the AI is autonomously discovering drugs?
unseenTransfer.answer: Apply the task-vs-authority split and the three questions. Which work was counted — likely bounded screening runs humans defined, not choosing which disease targets or candidate classes to pursue. What did the human still decide — probably the screening protocol, which hits to advance, and whether anything enters trials; running 70% of experiments inside a human-set pipeline is supervised execution, like Anthropic's 'led' level, not autonomy. Was the measure independently checked — a company counting its own runs with its own classifier is a preliminary internal measurement, so the percentage may not survive an external method. Conclusion: dramatic execution share, but authority over goals, evidence and deployment has not been shown to transfer.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: Correct reuse of the execution/authority distinction (P004), the retained human decision rights pattern (P005), and the three-question test with the independent-check caveat (P006, P008).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers cleanly to this new domain; the reader can resolve the scenario without any drug-discovery knowledge, confirming genuine transfer value.
